steps.name: header-spans-exactly-the-panels-beneath-it-and-adds-no-width
steps.addNotice: Placed H1: North wall — spans N1, N2, spanning 65½". Its name carries no direction — every header in the building is numbered in one H series, so H1 may be on one wall and H2 on another.

steps.name: a-one-panel-span-is-refused-and-changes-nothing
steps.notice: Refused: a spanning header has to sit on at least two panels. A header above ONE panel is already a panel of its own — set that panel's type instead. Nothing was changed.

steps.name: a-span-past-12ft-is-refused-rather-than-the-range-widened
steps.notice: Refused: those panels span 160", and a header is built between 48" and 144" — a range Building Integrity has not confirmed yet, so it is not widened to fit a drawing. Nothing was changed.

steps.name: deleting-a-panel-left-of-the-header-moves-its-range-not-its-span
steps.deleteNotice: Deleted a panel on wall AB: 17 panels → 16, 12 still automatic. Spanning header H1 still spans its panels, but those panels are now a different width: it is cut 81½" instead of 80".

steps.name: a-stop-that-would-re-cut-a-header-is-refused-by-name
steps.message: Refused: stopping this wall there would take panels out from under spanning header H1. A header's own width is the panels it spans, so shortening the wall would silently re-cut it. Remove the header first, or stop the wall somewhere else. Nothing was changed. (Esc to revert)
